newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says embassy in Kabul still functioning.
newsitem.headline: Iran says embassy in Kabul still functioning.

text.p: Iran said on Wednesday its embassy in Kabul, captured by the conservative Islamic Taleban last month, was still staffed and carrying out its functions, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
It quoted an informed source at the Foreign Ministry as saying reports of the departure of Iranian diplomats from the Afghan capital were incorrect.

"The source told IRNA on Wednesday that the Iranian embassy will continue to carry on its activities in the Afghan capital as long as conditions for function of the Iranian diplomats exist in the city," IRNA said.
The source did not say how many diplomats worked at the embassy or if any had left.
IRNA reported on Tuesday that all but one of Iran's diplomats had left their embassy in Kabul. It said the diplomats had gone to other parts of Afghanistan or to Pakistan over the last few days.
The agency, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, said in its Tuesday report that it was the first time in recent years that Iran had reduced its diplomatic corps in Kabul.

Iran recognises the ousted Afghan government of Burhanuddin Rabbani, driven out of Kabul by the Taleban. Iranian media has condemned Taleban as manipulated by the United States, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.
Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Tuesday the turmoil in Afghanistan threatened Iran's national security.
Afghanistan's new Sunni Moslem rulers have said neighbouring Iran continued to provoke the Taleban government despite recent assurances that relations would improve.
